summary: Researched Ben Davis's public pi coding agent setup by locating and inspecting the davis7dotsh/my-pi-setup repository, related YouTube walkthroughs, and his davis7.sh site. Documented repo structure, install flow, skill/extension/theme management, and notable UX patterns (ambient dashboard, async work, interactive control planes, structured clarification, workflow DSL). No files were edited.
decisions: Primary reference is the my-pi-setup repo cloned to ~/.pi/agent, with auto-discovered extensions/, skills/, and themes/ directories — chosen because the harness loads those paths on next start.

Capability/policy pairing: complex extensions (background-terminals, subagents) ship alongside matching SKILL.md files, so the extension provides tools while the skill defines usage policy — a separation the report treats as a key borrowable pattern.

Runtime state and credentials (sessions/, auth.json, settings.json, models.json, trust.json, .env, extensions/summaries/config.private.json) are gitignored, so the shareable repo contains behavior only and excludes machine-specific state.
Repo has no detected license and Ben explicitly discourages wholesale copying, so the output recommends using patterns as inspiration rather than redistributing code verbatim.

Multi-harness delegation: a single subagent interface routes work to Pi, Claude Code, or Codex with shared reasoning-effort controls and a concurrency cap — identified as the unified delegation pattern.
errors: Several search engines (brave, duckduckgo, startpage, google cse, wikipedia) were unresponsive due to CAPTCHA or rate-limiting, returning no results for some queries.
